requirement_text.ISS-0292: Fix for SandboxPoolTest RT-9/RT-8 CI flake. Change is confined to test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs's private cleanup helpers -- adds a single retry around a Repo.query!, and makes the DROP-schema cleanup loop attempt every schema instead of aborting on first failure. See lib/letflow/design/iss0292-sandbox-pool-test-cleanup-resilience.md Section 9 for full design, commit 23273a4c0791b645d4aafb0b0a26ea898aaab479 on branch feature/WF03-ISS0292-20260823 for the implementation.

task.description: Security review the diff on commit 23273a4c0791b645d4aafb0b0a26ea898aaab479 (branch feature/WF03-ISS0292-20260823) against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md. This is TEST-ONLY code (no lib/, no migration, no config/*.exs, no tenant-data path in the shipped application) -- confirm that scope claim yourself via `git show 23273a4c0791b645d4aafb0b0a26ea898aaab479 --stat`, then assess whether anything in the actual diff nonetheless touches a tenant-data invariant (it manipulates real Postgres schemas via DROP SCHEMA, so confirm the schema-name source is still the same test-only sandbox_% pattern already in use, not attacker/user-controlled input, and that no behavior change here could affect production tenant isolation).
acceptance_criteria: Confirms via git show --stat that only test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs changed
Confirms DROP SCHEMA targets remain sourced from the existing sandbox_% schema-name enumeration, not any new input path
States explicitly whether this diff has any tenant-data-path implication for the shipped application (expected: no, since it's test-only)

result.summary: Confirmed via `git show 23273a4c0791b645d4aafb0b0a26ea898aaab479 --stat` that only test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs (application-scope) plus a new handoff json changed -- no lib/, no priv/repo/migrations/, no config/*.exs. Scope test: not a tenant-data path (no API route, no migration, no secret resolution, no response-shaping, no lookup-by-ID handler) -- this is test-only cleanup-helper code. Assessed each invariant: INV-1 (tenant data isolation) NOT-APPLICABLE -- no Ecto schema module, business table, or migration touched; the sandbox_% schemas this file manipulates are test-fixture Postgres schemas, not tenant business-data schemas under 0003's scoping mechanism. INV-2 NOT-APPLICABLE (S4 not started, no API response type touched). INV-3 NOT-APPLICABLE (S5 not started). INV-4 (secrets) NOT-APPLICABLE -- no secret material read, logged, or serialized; Logger.warning calls only include schema names and Exception.format output, no credentials. INV-5 NOT-APPLICABLE (S4 not started, no lookup-by-ID endpoint). INV-6 (new data-access paths prove scoping) NOT-APPLICABLE -- no new data-access path; this restructures existing test cleanup control flow only. INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) APPLIES (Repo.query! present) -- verified PASS: the DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS "#{schema_name}" CASCADE interpolation is pre-existing (confirmed identical in the pre-commit blob, only relocated into the new resilient_drop_schema/1 helper, not newly introduced), and schema_name is sourced exclusively from sandbox_schema_names/0's SELECT against information_schema.schemata with a hardcoded LIKE 'sandbox\_%' literal (no caller/tenant/network input reaches this value) -- confirmed via `git show <sha>:test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs | grep -n sandbox_schema_names` that every call site of the DROP path traces back to this same internal enumeration. No new injection surface. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes) APPLIES (Postgrex/DBConnection calls touch external I/O) -- verified PASS: this diff is a net improvement, converting a bare `for` loop that aborted on first crash into a typed {:ok|:error}-shaped Enum.reduce/3 fold (resilient_drop_schema/1 returns {:error, exception} instead of raising, mirroring test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex's reclaim_row/1 shape) plus a bounded single retry in retry_query_once/1; failures still surface loudly via one combined flunk/1 rather than going silent. No production shared-process path is touched -- this is ExUnit test teardown code, not lib/. No tenant-data-path implication for the shipped application: confirmed, this diff cannot affect production tenant isolation since it touches only test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs's private cleanup helpers.
